subject: QBridge SOW — executive concurrence required for warranty & indemnity redlines
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@qbridge.io>, procurement@qbridge.io
Date: Fri, 01 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Waiver request — warranty & indemnity adjustments for QBridge SOW

Kim and Laura,

Attaching the latest QBridge redline (v3). They have pushed to remove the standard warranty paragraph and want an indemnity carveout for third-party claims relating to integrations (they've added a clause that effectively removes our defense obligations for partner-supplied connectors). Procurement says this is a make-or-break for their executive council — they want the SOW signed this week.

Highlights: 
- Warranty: deliverables warranty language removed; QBridge wants "as-is" except for gross negligence.
- Indemnity: significantly expanded for their partners; they propose we indemnify for claims even when caused by partner integrations.
- Liability cap: they asked that cap be removed for IP claims and for partner-related incidents.

I flagged to Laura that this is high risk. Pricing team is offering a 25% upfront discount to compensate if we accept some concessions, but that would require executive approval. Can you review and advise next steps?

Attachments: QBridge_SOW_v3_redline.docx

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@qbridge.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Dec 2028 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Waiver request — warranty & indemnity adjustments for QBridge SOW

Ben —
Quick clarification from our side: the request is not to remove all warranty, but to limit warranties to "material" defects and to avoid broad carve-ins that would expose our partners. On indemnity: our legal team is asking for mutuality around third-party claims for partner-made connectors; we are willing to accept a liability cap tied to first-year committed fees rather than an unlimited position.

We understand you have internal constraints. We have an internal approval window closing Friday EOD for budget planning. Can your team confirm whether an exec-level tradeoff (discount + modified cap structure) is feasible?

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Procurement — QBridge
elena@qbridge.io
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Dec 2028 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Waiver request — warranty & indemnity adjustments for QBridge SOW

Ben/Team,

Reviewed the redline attached. Summary of legal risk (see attached PDF for full matrix):
- Removing the warranty leaves us exposed on delivery and performance claims; we would lose key contractual remedies.
- The indemnity language as drafted would require us to cover partner-originated losses without clear causation thresholds; unacceptable without severe limits or indemnity carveouts.
- Liability cap removal for IP-related claims materially increases our enterprise risk profile.

Potential compromise (legal recommendation):
1) Keep a limited warranty for delivery/performance (90 days) tied to a "material defect" standard.
2) Mutual indemnity for third-party claims arising out of integrations; if we indemnify, require clear causation buckets and require partner contributory indemnity.
3) Liability cap: allow a narrow exception for IP indemnity (we can accept carveouts) but cap exposure to 12 months of recurring committed fees (deal_id: QB-2028-1147) rather than no cap.

Given the financial tradeoffs, this will need exec concurrence. Included a risk summary (QBridge_Risk_Summary_v2.pdf). If Sales wants to offer a commercial concession (discount or extended term), indicate amount and I will draft a redline.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Attachments: QBridge_Risk_Summary_v2.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Dec 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Waiver request — warranty & indemnity adjustments for QBridge SOW

Markus —
Forwarding. Ben says QBridge will pull the PO if they don't get traction this week. Laura's recommendations are solid, but we should decide commercial levers quickly. Pricing has floated 25% upfront and a 12-month fee cap per Laura's note. From a go-to-market perspective, this is a strategic reference for the healthcare vertical and could open a larger partnership.

Ask: can you confirm whether you're comfortable with the following package for exec sign-off?
- Liability cap: capped at 12 months of committed fees (per deal math) with explicit IP carveout exceptions handled by Legal.
- Warranty: limited material-defect warranty (90 days).
- Indemnity: mutual indemnity for partner integrations with causation thresholds + partner contributory indemnity.
- Commercial concession: 20% upfront discount (compromise from pricing).

If you agree, I'll loop in the CFO/CEO for an official sign-off and get DocuSign ready. If you'd prefer a different commercial offset please suggest.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Dec 2028 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Waiver request — warranty & indemnity adjustments for QBridge SOW

Kim —
I support the proposed package with one modification: make the upfront commercial concession 20% (agreed) but structure it as a time-limited credit applied against year-one committed usage (so we retain some revenue protection). Also want a hard stop: if they request additional unlimited carveouts during implementation, we reserve the right to pause integrations until a remediation plan is agreed.

Please proceed to get exec concurrence. I'll be available for a quick sync with the CEO if needed — we should keep the ask tight and include a one-page executive summary that focuses on strategic value vs. delta to ARR.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 09:55:00 -0800
Subject: Executive memo + requested sign-off language for QBridge (QB-2028-1147)

Kim/Markus/Ben —
Attached is a one-page executive memo and a clean contract excerpt that implements the compromise:
- Warranty: 90-day limited material-defect warranty.
- Indemnity: mutual indemnity for third-party claims tied to demonstrable causation; requires partner contributory indemnity.
- Liability cap: general cap of 12 months committed fees; IP indemnity remains excluded only where we are found to have infringed third-party IP (narrow carveout).
- Commercial: 20% upfront credit applied to year-one committed usage; conditional on signature by EOD Friday.

If you approve, I will prepare a DocuSign packet and the sign-off request to the CEO. Suggested approval language for the CEO to sign: \"I approve an exception to standard contract risk tolerances for QBridge (deal QB-2028-1147), limited to the terms summarized in the attached memo. This approval is conditioned on execution of the attached redline and the commercial credit structure described.\"

Please reply with "APPROVE" or "DECLINE" and any edits; if APPROVE I will route to the CEO with the DocuSign link.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
